URL where issue was found: 

I'm including places where this information could be explicitly stated so users know ipv6 is required for the discovery application to run (I believe it just needs to be enabled at the kernel level)l:

Description of issue: 

When the  ipv6 protocol is completely disabled, the discovery application fails to start.

We can see error messages with nginx like so:

{code}
 Apr 10 00:37:28 dnvapprhdiscovr.corp.entsec.com discovery-app[2577]: nginx: [emerg] socket() [::]:8079 failed (97: Address family not supported by protocol)
{code}


The containers are in a continuous cycle trying to start.  We see the first 4 containers get started:

%code%
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE                                                     COMMAND               CREATED                 STATUS                 PORTS              NAMES
d990e6d75d2f  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-15:latest             run-postgresql        1 second ago            Up 1 second            5432/tcp           discovery-db
07c871840103  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/redis-6:latest                   run-redis             1 second ago            Up 1 second            6379/tcp           discovery-redis
8b00dba8cec3  registry.redhat.io/discovery/discovery-server-rhel9:1.13  /bin/bash /deploy...  Less than a second ago  Up 1 second            443/tcp, 8000/tcp  discovery-server
9fd605a3a9d1  registry.redhat.io/discovery/discovery-server-rhel9:1.13  /bin/sh -c /deplo...  Less than a second ago  Up Less than a second  443/tcp            discovery-celery-worker
%code%


Then the "discovery-celery-worker" container dies almost instantly:

%code%
[rexuser@lb1 ~]$ podman ps
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE                                                     COMMAND               CREATED        STATUS        PORTS              NAMES
d990e6d75d2f  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-15:latest             run-postgresql        3 seconds ago  Up 3 seconds  5432/tcp           discovery-db
07c871840103  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/redis-6:latest                   run-redis             3 seconds ago  Up 3 seconds  6379/tcp           discovery-redis
8b00dba8cec3  registry.redhat.io/discovery/discovery-server-rhel9:1.13  /bin/bash /deploy...  2 seconds ago  Up 3 seconds  443/tcp, 8000/tcp  discovery-server
%code%

Finally around 12 seconds in, only the first 2 containers are running (discovery-db and discovery-redis):

%code%
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE                                          COMMAND         CREATED         STATUS         PORTS       NAMES
d990e6d75d2f  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-15:latest  run-postgresql  12 seconds ago  Up 12 seconds  5432/tcp    discovery-db
07c871840103  registry.redhat.io/rhel9/redis-6:latest        run-redis       12 seconds ago  Up 12 seconds  6379/tcp    discovery-redis
%code%

And after about 22 seconds total time, the containers are restarted, and it continues this way.
